transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I ain't. I know for a fact they’ve been watching my moves on the floor and changing the pallet counts on my logs just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

It’s always on the loading dock, too, with those big heavy wooden pallets. The ones that give you splinters right through your work gloves if you aren't careful. I actually had to buy a new pair of leather ones from the hardware store down on 4th street last week. The guy who runs that place is real nice, he always gives me a discount because I went to high school with his daughter for a couple years before I left. She had this really loud laugh, kind of like a goose honking, you know? Anyway, I was telling my husband about the gloves and he just rolled his eyes at me. He’s been spending all his time in the driveway messing with his truck engine anyway, leaving his tools all over the grass... I don't even know why he made me come here today.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

Well, yeah, I guess. Like sometimes when I'm in the aisle at work or just at home folding clothes, I hear a man's voice clear as day saying Nicole check it again, even when nobody is near me. It happens when I'm doing the laundry a lot. Which is a real chore because my husband gets grease all over his jeans from messing with that truck of his, and I have to scrub them in the sink with that gritty orange soap before I even put them in the machine. It smells exactly like the hand soap they used to have at the roller rink off Highway 9. Man, I used to go skating there every Friday night when I was fifteen. They had this DJ who played all the best music, and we’d get those big soft pretzels with the hot plastic cheese. I burned the roof of my mouth on that cheese once so bad I couldn't taste my food for a whole week. My mom made meatloaf that Sunday and I couldn't even taste the ketchup on it, which is a shame because she made a really good glaze. But anyway, yeah, there's never anybody standing there when the man tells me to check things.
Have you had any periods—lasting a week or more—where your mood was much lower than usual, or unusually high, energetic, or irritable, separate from these experiences at work?

Well, yeah, sometimes I get this feeling where I'm just so fired up, like I've got all this energy and absolutely nobody can slow me down. I get so much done around the house, but then my husband will ask me just one tiny little question about the kids or what my schedule is for the week, and I just snap at him. It feels like he's trying to control every little thing I do, you know? 

Just like how he’s always trying to tell me how to organize the garage. He’s got all those heavy wrenches and socket sets for that truck engine, and he just leaves them scattered all over my workbench. I bought that workbench at a yard sale a couple years ago. It was from this older couple who were moving down to Florida, I think to Orlando or maybe Tampa. They had this beautiful golden retriever puppy running around the yard while we were loading it into the back of my cousin's truck. My cousin has this old Chevy Silverado, the paint is peeling right off the hood, but it runs like a dream. We actually took it camping up by the lake last summer and caught three huge catfish. But yeah, if my husband even looks at me wrong when I'm feeling that fired up, I just lose it on him.

Do you ever hear that man's voice or feel like your husband and coworkers are watching or plotting against you even during times when your mood feels completely normal—not unusually high-energy or low?

Yeah, I still hear him even when things are calm. Like, a couple months ago, I had this stretch for a few weeks where I wasn't running around like a crazy person, and I was actually sleeping pretty normal. But I still heard that guy's voice telling me to check things, and I still knew for a fact they were messing with my pallet counts. 

It's just so frustrating because I'm the one who organizes the pallets by the loading dock doors, and I always make sure the blue ones from Chep are stacked separate from the plain wood ones. Those blue ones are heavier, you know? They paint them that color so you know they belong to the company and you can't just take them home to build stuff. My neighbor, Gary, he actually took a bunch of old pallets once and built this whole compost bin in his backyard. He grows these massive tomatoes, like the size of softballs. He gave me a basket of them last August and I made my own salsa. I put way too much jalapeño in it, though, and my husband was sweating just eating it with tortilla chips while he was watching the football game. He always watches the games in his recliner, the one with the duct tape on the armrest where the cat scratched it up... but yeah, even when my mood is totally fine and I'm just doing my job, I know they're plotting against me and I still hear the voice.

Over the entire time you've been hearing this voice and believing people are plotting against you—let's say however many months or years that's been—would you say those 'fired up' high-energy episodes have been happening most of that time, or have they been a relatively small part of it compared to how long the voice and suspicious feelings have been going on?

Well, if I look back at all the time since this whole thing started, I'd say those fired-up times have been happening for more than half of it. It's like I get going and I hardly sleep at all, and I just keep taking on more and more stuff. And then I get so mad if anyone tries to slow me down. Like last week, I decided I was going to clean out the gutters, even though it was already getting dark. You really have to stay on top of the gutters because if the leaves pile up, the water just pours right over the edge and ruins the flower beds. I planted these beautiful marigolds last spring, the bright orange ones. They say marigolds keep the bugs away from your other plants, but I still saw a bunch of Japanese beetles chewing on my rose bushes. My grandma used to have this trick where she'd put out a little dish of soapy water to catch them. She lived in this tiny house with a wrap-around porch, and we'd sit out there snapping green beans in the summer. She made the best green bean casserole for Thanksgiving, not with that canned soup, she made her own sauce from scratch with fresh mushrooms. I tried to make it once, but I burned the butter in the pan, and the whole house smelled like smoke for two days. I had to open all the windows, and it was freezing outside because it was November. But yeah, those high-energy stretches where I'm doing way too much and snapping at people, that's been going on for most of the time I've been dealing with the voice and the pallets.
Aside from these high-energy, fired-up periods, have you also had separate stretches lasting a week or more where you felt unusually down, hopeless, or lacking energy?

No, I don't really get down like that. I mean, sure, sometimes I'm tired after a long shift, but I don't have whole weeks where I'm just sitting around hopeless or anything. If I did that, the house would fall apart. You know, you have to stay on top of the laundry, especially with the kids' soccer uniforms. They get so muddy, especially when it rains the night before a game. Last time they played, the field was basically a swamp, and my youngest slipped and slid right into the goalpost. He was fine, just a little bruise, but the grass stains on those white shorts... I tried soaking them in OxiClean overnight, but it didn't even make a dent. My sister told me to use this special paste she makes with baking soda and vinegar, she swears by it. She's always coming up with these little home remedies. Like when I had a sore throat last winter, she made me drink this hot water with lemon, honey, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. It burned going down, but it actually worked pretty fast. We used to drink hot cocoa with those tiny marshmallows when we were kids after playing in the snow all day. But no, I haven't really had any periods where I felt super down or hopeless like you're talking about.
